articles.title: Michael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fate
articles.summary: Head coach arrives to watch under-21s play. Bruno Fernandes likes Instagram post about loyalty. Michael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday afternoon as elsewhere at the Carrington base Jason Wilcox, the sporting director, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, deliberated…
body: Carrick arrived at about 1.50pm to watch the under-21s play a behind-closed-doors game.

Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington on Monday morning after United’s 3-0 loss to Bournemouth on Sunday at Old Trafford that left Carrick’s job in the balance. Wilcox departed just before 5pm and Carrick went shortly after.
The defeat made it eight games without a win for Carrick’s side, who have two victories all season. United are in 16th in the Premier League, a point above the relegation zone.

If the 45-year-old is removed, Eddie Howe remains Wilcox’s preferred candidate, with contact between them understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations.

articles.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at the Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points. José Mourinho had already done the por qu é?, the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days.
body: He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600km west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out.

articles.title: Fearnley retires injured to give Fery victory at Vienna Open
articles.summary: Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.
body: Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss.
Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition.
Fery will face the winner of No 6 seed Francis Tiafoe and Lorenzo Musetti - the latter of whom he lost against in straight sets at the US Open - in the second round.

articles.title: Doubles players sign open letter pleading with tennis chiefs to ‘protect’ format
articles.summary: Plans to slash games by half and prize money criticised. ‘Hard for players to build and sustain a doubles career’ More than 150 doubles players on the men’s ATP tour have signed an open letter addressed to the ATP board and management imploring the men’s tennis governing bodies to reconsider…
body: The subject of potential reforms to the ATP has been a significant issue since players were informed in a meeting during Wimbledon that the ATP was conducting a review of its doubles regulations and potential changes could see doubles draws being halved at the ATP events in 2028. Under these proposals, ATP Masters 1000 events would host only 16 doubles teams and the main draws at ATP 500 and 250 events would accommodate only eight teams.

The proposals could also lead to the total prize money distributed to doubles players being halved from 20% to 10%, with the remaining money allocated towards singles players. The news provoked significant criticism from a large group of doubles players at Wimbledon, and they have spent subsequent months organising to resist the reforms. In addition to over 150 active players, the letter has been signed by more than 20 national federations and legends of the sport.

articles.title: Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille?
articles.summary: Lille’s results under Carlo’s son in Ligue 1 are encouraging but they have been exposed in the Champions League. By Get French Football News. In a restaurant in Rio de Janeiro, two aspiring young managers sit around a table.
body: Speaking before his first meeting with Ancelotti in Ligue 1 on Sunday, the Monaco manager, Filipe Luís, described his counterpart at Lille as a “really formidable person”. The Brazilian added: “It is something special for us. It will be a pleasure to face my friend.”

There were 12 managerial appointments in Ligue 1 over the summer; Filipe Luís and Ancelotti were two of the most interesting. Filipe Luís won the Premier League with Chelsea but is probably best known in Europe for his eight years at Atlético Madrid, where he won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and two Europa League titles across two spells. He carried on that success in his first job as a manager, winning the Copa Libertadores with Flamengo. “He knows what he’s talking about and how to motivate us,” says the Monaco forward Matthis Abline. “It motivates us even more to have a manager like him behind us.”

articles.title: Celtic & Rangers wait for stadium closures ruling
articles.summary: Rangers and Celtic submit appeals against a ruling that they must play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors following scenes of disorder in last season's competition.
body: Rangers and Celtic are waiting for a Scottish FA appellate tribunal to rule on their respective appeals against an order that they must play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors.
The Glasgow clubs presented their cases on Monday and the tribunal will now undertake a period of deliberation before announcing whether the sanctions stand.
The stadium closure penalty was announced in late August following the disorder at the end of last season's quarter-final tie at Ibrox, which Celtic won after a penalty shoot-out.
They clubs are also challenging fines of £100,000 after their fans clashed on the Ibrox pitch.

articles.title: England-Republic of Ireland U15 World Cup game ends over alleged racism
articles.summary: The Under-15 World Cup Group C match between England and Republic of Ireland is abandoned after England allege an opposition player made a racist comment.
body: England walked off the pitch during a match at the Under-15 World Cup after an allegation of racism by a Republic of Ireland player, which resulted in the game being abandoned.
Following an altercation between players from both sides, shortly before the end of the match in Azerbaijan on Monday, an England player approached his bench and made a complaint to coaching staff.
Match footage then showed England staff members relaying the complaint to the referee, alleging a racist slur had been said, and calling their players off.
Republic of Ireland were leading 4-1 at the time of the incident.

articles.title: Makin wants to be Liverpool's next great champion
articles.summary: Middleweight Callum Makin has excelled for the GB boxing team, but his Olympic future rests on a decision.
body: Makin has won medals for Britain at both the World and European championships at 75kgs. But, with Olympic qualification looming next year, he has to choose his weight category.
With 75kgs no longer an Olympic weight Makin has to move up or move down by five kilos.
Although he became a national champion twice over at light-middleweight, Makin expects to bulk up for his Olympic qualification campaign.
"It's either 70 or 80kgs for me, which is a massive jump either side," Makin told Sky Sports.

articles.title: 'Cutting doubles would destroy careers' - angry players urge ATP rethink
articles.summary: More than 150 doubles players - including Wimbledon champions and tennis legends - urge the ATP to rethink "drastic" cuts which they believe could kill the format.
body: In a show of collective action, the players have written an open letter to the men's governing body as they fight proposals which would cut draw sizes and reduce prize money from 2028.
"We're at risk of losing a discipline of tennis which is historic - but has a big future," Dutch player Sem Verbeek, one of the architects of the letter, told BBC Sport.
The ATP proposed halving the doubles draws at its flagship Masters 1000 events to 16 teams, with smaller tournaments reduced to eight teams.
The percentage of prize money devoted to doubles could fall from 20% to 10% - with the difference redistributed to singles players.

articles.title: Careers on the line for Australia in deciding South Africa Test?
articles.summary: Australia are about to play a Test match in Cape Town for the first time since the ball-tampering scandal back in 2018 that paused a number of their cricketers' careers.
body: Should they lose to South Africa this week in the series decider, live on Sky Sports Cricket, a number of careers could be ended.
Having been humbled by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha last time out, a game in which they were torpedoed for 99 in the first innings, the Baggy Greens need a response.
If that does not come, the reaction from the Australian media could be more abrasive than the piece of sandpaper Cameron Bancroft aimed to conceal down his trousers eight years ago.

In the 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, it was held together by Travis Head, Steve Smith and Alex Carey as others toiled, while in South Africa so far the tourists have managed only three individual fifty-plus scores - one for Head and two for Matt Renshaw.

articles.title: Cameron Young was closer to joining LIV Golf than anyone knew
articles.summary: In 2022, Cameron Young acknowledged he had seriously considered leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf. What he didn’t reveal was just how close he came. New bankruptcy records filed by LIV Golf show Young had signed an offer of intent with the breakaway league before ultimately deciding to remain with…
body: Young’s near-departure is one of several revelations contained in the financial records, which offer a deeper look at the money LIV spent on players and executives before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Sept. 8.

"Obviously it's the elephant in the room for everyone. Frankly, throughout the whole process with (LIV Golf), I was very interested. I think they have a bunch of good ideas and are doing some cool stuff," Young said in August 2022. "With some of the changes coming (to the PGA Tour), that's kind of what really helped me decide to kind of stay and pursue those goals that I have for myself like making a Presidents Cup team and a Ryder Cup team and winning a major, when all of that is just uncertain if you go. That's a tough place for me because, you know, I'm very young and there are a lot of factors."

Ultimately, Young stayed with the PGA Tour and has since won three times, including the 2026 Players Championship. He stands second on the 2026 PGA Tour money list with more than $15 million in earnings.
points: In 2022, Cameron Young acknowledged he had seriously considered leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf.
What he didn’t reveal was just how close he came.
"Obviously it's the elephant in the room for everyone.
I think they have a bunch of good ideas and are doing some cool stuff," Young said in August 2022.

articles.title: Francisco Lindor Wins 2026 Roberto Clemente Award, Continuing a Proud Puerto Rican Legacy
articles.summary: Francisco Lindor won the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award for his philanthropy, youth mentorship and community work in Puerto Rico and New York. New York Mets star Francisco Lindor has won MLB's 2026 Roberto Clemente Award.
body: Francisco Lindor has accomplished just about everything a baseball player could hope to achieve. He’s a five-time All-Star, a four-time Silver Slugger and one of the most recognizable shortstops in Major League Baseball.
But on October 26, Lindor received an honor that has little to do with his numbers at the plate or his performance on the field.
The New York Mets star was named the 2026 recipient of the Roberto Clemente Award, Major League Baseball’s highest individual honor for a player’s character, philanthropy and community impact.

For Lindor, the recognition carries an additional layer of meaning. He’s a proud Puerto Rican native who grew up learning about Clemente, the legendary Hall of Famer whose impact on baseball extended far beyond the diamond.

articles.title: Verstappen fumes at Red Bull radio dropouts during races
articles.summary: Max Verstappen says technical issues with Red Bull's team radio are "a disaster" after he struggled to communicate with his engineer for a second successive race.
body: On his way to finishing third in Sunday's United States Grand Prix, Verstappen was trying to let the Red Bull pit wall know he was suffering from engine braking issues.
When his engineer attempted to offer him advice by suggesting a change of mode, Verstappen said that he couldn't hear him properly.
The issue appeared to be similar to the one Verstappen suffered two weeks earlier when he and the pit wall were forced to improvise their communication methods during his win in Singapore.
Speaking after Sunday's race in Austin, Verstappen said: "It's not the second time. It's already, I don't know how many times this year.
